questions.question: How many samples does simulate_chunk(True, rng) create with the default 20 ms chunk and 16 kHz rate?
What does rms_dbfs convert into decibels?
options: The maximum sample using 10*log10
The root-mean-square amplitude using 20*log10
The number of samples using a natural logarithm
The mean frequency bin in hertz
questions.explanation: It computes RMS, clamps it at 1e-10, and applies 20*log10.

questions.question: When does vad(chunk, threshold_dbfs=-40) return True?
options: When the chunk has exactly 320 samples
When the chunk contains any zero sample
When the chunk RMS level is strictly above -40 dBFS
When its peak frequency is 40 Hz
questions.explanation: vad delegates to rms_dbfs and compares the result with > threshold_dbfs.

questions.question: What latency does fake_stt use for a 2-second buffered utterance?
options: 250 ms
80 ms
100 ms
180 ms
questions.explanation: The formula is 80 + 2*50 = 180 milliseconds before the sleep.

questions.question: What does fake_tts_first_audio represent in the pipeline?
options: Time to first audio chunk, simulated as a 100 ms wait
Time to render the entire conversation waveform
The VAD hangover duration
The number of text tokens returned by the LLM
questions.explanation: The function sleeps 0.10 seconds and returns a placeholder audio chunk, modeling TTFA.

questions.question: Why is measuring stage latency separately useful for a real-time agent?
options: It guarantees that speech recognition has zero errors
It reveals which component consumes the latency budget instead of hiding all waits in one total
It replaces the need for audio buffering
It makes a sequential pipeline full duplex automatically
questions.explanation: The demo records STT, LLM, and TTS timings so an operator can target the largest contributor.
